subject: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

Hey Alex/Marissa — want to lock down TTFS definition + data sources this week so telemetry + dashboard work doesn’t drift.

Proposed working definition (Hosted API):
1) TTFS (“time to first success”): time from tenant_created_at (first successful signup / tenant provisioned) → first successful inference response observed server-side.
   - “first successful inference response” = first gateway-handled request that returns HTTP 2xx from any of:
     - /v1/chat.completions
     - /v1/responses
     - /v1/embeddings
     - /v1/rerank
   - Must have an authenticated API key (so we’re not counting 401/403) and must not be an internal health check.
   - Question: do we require >0 output tokens (chat/responses) or is 2xx sufficient? (Embeddings is always “0 output tokens” in the same sense.)

2) Attribution: we should attribute TTFS to the “first client surface” where possible (SDK vs OpenAI-compat vs raw HTTP).
   - Inputs I think we can reliably use: user-agent tags (SDKs + openai-compat), request headers (x-redwood-client), and gateway route.
   - Question: if the first success comes from the Console “try it” panel, do we want that to count as TTFS? My gut: yes (it’s a success moment), but separate breakdown.

3) Data source & lag:
   - For the metric itself I’m leaning on gateway-side event emission → onboarding events table (so we aren’t depending on usage dashboard/billing aggregation latency).
   - We still need to reconcile with billing/usage for validation.
   - Open issue: Support tickets show confusion when Usage dashboard lags (SUP-18544). That shouldn’t affect TTFS, but will cause perceived mismatch.

Decision points:
A) Anchor timestamp: tenant_created_at vs first API key created_at (some people create keys before making a call).
B) What counts as “first success” across endpoints (2xx only vs additional checks).
C) Whether Console “try it” counts in headline TTFS or only in a breakout.

If we align on this thread, I’ll update PM-751 and the KPI dashboard spec.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Director PM, Hosted API
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 10:04 AM PT
Subject: Re: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

+1 to locking this now.

Two Console-specific questions:
- Our checklist “First API call” step is currently planned to flip to complete off server-side event(s). If TTFS is computed from those same events, we should make sure the event semantics don’t accidentally exclude the Console try-it panel. Otherwise we’ll show “step complete” but TTFS still missing (or vice versa).
- For perceived lag: the Usage dashboard today can lag (esp. when people test in bursts). Even if TTFS is independent, users will compare. Should we add a small note in the checklist step detail (“usage metrics may take up to X minutes”) and/or link to the troubleshooting doc?

On the definition: I’d prefer we anchor to tenant_created_at (signup moment). If someone generates an API key and never makes a call, TTFS should stay null.

Marissa
Dir PM, Console


---

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 11:22 AM PT
Subject: Re: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

Aligning with Marissa on anchoring to tenant_created_at.

My votes to close the open items:
A) Anchor: tenant_created_at.
B) First success criteria:
   - Use “first 2xx from supported inference endpoints” and don’t add token-based requirements.
   - Reason: embeddings/rerank are real success paths and we shouldn’t bias to generation only.
   - But: exclude internal probes and exclude “validation” endpoints (if any).
C) Console try-it:
   - Count it in TTFS. It’s still a success moment and reduces friction.
   - Add dimension in reporting: first_success_surface = {console_tryit, sdk, openai_compat, raw_http, unknown}

Re: dashboard lag — we should treat as separate “data freshness UX” item, but I do want us to proactively message it. Let’s include a concise note in checklist copy and link to the troubleshooting article. This should also reduce SUP-18544 style tickets.

Action: Nikhil, please update PM-751 with the above. Marissa/Dylan: ensure the event(s) emitted can include surface attribution (at least “console_tryit” vs everything else).

Alex
VP Developer Experience

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 12:10 PM PT
Subject: Re: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

Works for Console.

Implementation note: we can tag Console try-it traffic in a couple ways:
- We already set a distinct user-agent for the in-console client.
- We can also add x-redwood-client=console_tryit so it survives proxying/UA normalization.

For the checklist step state: if TTFS is derived from the same gateway events, it should line up as long as:
- The event is emitted after 2xx is returned (not at request start), and
- We key it on (tenant_id, endpoint_category) with an idempotency key to avoid duplicates.

On the “usage dashboard may lag” note — we can add it in the step drawer copy (small callout) + link.

Dylan
Eng Lead, Console & Tooling

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 2:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

Great — thanks all. Summarizing the decision for PM-751/PM-742:

TTFS (headline metric):
- Start: tenant_created_at (tenant provisioned / signup completed)
- End: first server-observed 2xx response from supported inference endpoints (chat/responses/embeddings/rerank)
- Exclusions: internal probes/health checks; non-inference endpoints
- Null if no success event

Attribution (required dimension): first_success_surface
- console_tryit
- sdk (python/ts/go/etc.)
- openai_compat
- raw_http
- unknown

Data source:
- Server-side event emission at gateway/control plane (not derived from usage dashboard). Validation will compare against usage/billing aggregates.

Open items I’ll capture as follow-ups:
1) Define “internal probes” filter list (routes + UA patterns) so we don’t contaminate TTFS.
2) Decide the “max acceptable delay” language for the checklist copy (e.g., “up to ~15 minutes”). I’d like to confirm with telemetry pipeline owners before we hardcode.

Marissa/Dylan — if you have preferred wording for the lag note, send and I’ll align with Support too.

Nikhil

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 4:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: TTFS metric definition alignment (onboarding checklist / Hosted API)

Suggested checklist copy for the lag note (step drawer under “View usage”):

“Usage and cost dashboards update with a short delay (typically a few minutes). If you don’t see traffic reflected yet, wait a bit and refresh. For real-time debugging, check request logs/traces.”

We can link “request logs/traces” to the Console logging page and add a “Why is my usage delayed?” doc link once docs confirms the canonical URL.

Also +1 on having a concrete filter list for internal probes. If we can’t get it perfect on day 1, I’d rather keep it conservative (exclude obvious internal UAs, keep everything else).

Marissa
